audit.TITLE: Audit a live page
audit.LEAD: Paste a public URL and we'll run up to 246 automatic checks against it. You get a score, what to fix, and one click to tick the passing items in your checklist.
audit.LABEL: Page URL
audit.APPLY: Tick passing items in my checklist
audit.NOTE: Automatic checks cover only what can be verified from the page's HTML and response headers. Everything else, such as real-device testing or content quality, stays a manual item in the checklist. Only public pages can be audited.
audit.BRAND_TAGLINE: Websites, web apps and engineering support
audit.BRAND_CTA: Need help fixing these issues? Talk to Shinning Tech Services
audit.REPORT_DISCLAIMER: This is an automated, point-in-time scan of one public page. It reads the page's HTML, linked CSS/JS, images and response headers. It is a starting point for a review, not a certification, and it does not replace manual testing.
audit.HEURISTIC_NOTE: Items marked “verify” rely on heuristics (for example reading level, minification, thin content or script detection) and can be false positives or negatives. Confirm them manually before acting.
LIMITS: Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP) and other real-user or lab performance metrics. Only server response time, page weight and loading hints are checked.
Real-device, browser and screen-reader testing, and visual quality (layout, colour contrast in context, animation).
Content quality, tone, accuracy and legal wording. Only simple signals such as length and reading level are estimated.
Pages behind a login, forms, checkout and other interactive flows. Only the public page you submitted is fetched, with no JavaScript execution.
The Testing section of the checklist (unit, end-to-end, visual and load tests live in your codebase, not on the page).
Only one page is scanned; other pages of the site may differ.
audit.NOT_CHECKED_INTRO: Checklist items this scan did not decide. Review these manually:

help.TITLE: How to use this checklist
help.INTRO: A front-end quality checklist you can work through by hand or partly automate.

STEPS.title: 1. Work through the checklist.
STEPS.text: Open a section from the sidebar and tick items as you complete them. Click the arrow on an item for documentation and tools.

STEPS.title: 2. Filter what matters.
STEPS.text: Use the tag pills to focus on one area, and the eye icon to hide a section you don't need.

STEPS.title: 3. Audit a live page.
STEPS.text: On the Audit page, paste a URL. Up to 246 checks run automatically and the passing items can be ticked in your checklist in one click.

STEPS.title: 4. Generate a report.
STEPS.text: Open Report to fill in the project name and developer, then print or save a PDF of your progress.

TIPS: Your progress is saved in this browser only. Nothing is uploaded.
The dark/light button remembers your choice.
Use EN / FR in the top bar to switch language.
AI assistants can run the audit too: see the MCP server and agent skill in the GitHub repository.
